Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

(CNN)  -- The University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill student body president who was killed this year was shot several times, including in her head, according to her autopsy report released Monday. Unsealed warrants show Eve Carson was abducted and then shot by both men. Eve Carson, 22, was found slain on March 5. Carson's autopsy report lists six gunshot wounds, but says two were probably from the same bullet, according to North Carolina's Office of the Chief Medical Examiner. Carson's death shocked the community and drew national attention. An estimated 10,000 people turned out for a service remembering her. Her autopsy -- released after a North Carolina newspaper filed a court motion to have it unsealed -- describes wounds to various parts of Carson's body. It says shotgun wounds to her head and hand "most likely represent a single shot with the hand acting as an intermediate target." One of the other four wounds was also a gunshot to her head. A separate, handwritten summary of the medical examiner's report says Carson was "shot multiple times" and found lying on her back, with one arm bent behind her head. The autopsy says sexual assault testing was done. It does not say whether any sign of sexual assault was found. Two suspects, Demario James Atwater, 22, and Lawrence Alvin Lovette, 17, have been charged with first-degree murder. Lovette's attorney said the warrants against the suspects rely on hearsay. Atwater's attorney cautioned against "any rush to judgment." Court documents released Friday say Carson was kidnapped from her apartment and forced to provide her abductors with ATM access to her bank account before she was shot to death in the early hours of March 5. The documents -- applications for search warrants -- say a confidential informant told police in the days after the death that Atwater had told her he and Lovette had entered Carson's home through an open door and forced Carson to accompany them in her car. The informant said she had talked with Atwater after a picture was displayed on television showing someone attempting to use Carson's ATM card at a convenience store two days after Carson's body was found. The informant said the two men drove Carson to an ATM, obtaining her PIN number from her. "The CW [informant] learned that Carson was forced into the back seat with Atwater, and Lovette drove Carson's vehicle," the court documents said. "That information is consistent with video footage taken from an ATM camera on that date." The witness told police Atwater said the two got about $1,400 from Carson's account. Bank records show that was approximately the amount taken from the account over a two-day period, the documents said. And the informant said that both suspects shot Carson, according to one of the affidavits. "This information was corroborated by crime scene search information that two separate weapons were used in the homicide," the documents said. The documents said police believe Carson was subjected to a sexual assault "of an unknown nature" and asked for a search warrant to collect DNA swabs from the suspects. But Orange County, North Carolina, District Attorney Jim Woodall told CNN Friday the collection and testing done on Carson's body was routine, and authorities do not believe she was sexually assaulted. Prosecutors had fought to keep her autopsy sealed. Following a motion by the Raleigh News & Observer newspaper, prosecutors agreed to allow the report's release. Carson, a native of Athens, Georgia, was a pre-medicine student double-majoring in political science and biology. She was a recipient of the university's prestigious Morehead Scholarship and a member of the Phi Beta Kappa honor society, UNC has said.

Her killing stunned the community and received nationwide attention. About 10,000 people attended a memorial service in her honor.

It states that shotgun wounds to her head and hand “most likely represent a single shot with the hand acting as an intermediate target.” Another of the four remaining wounds was also a gunshot injury to the head.

In a separate handwritten summary, the medical examiner said Carson had been “shot multiple times.” She was discovered on her back, with one arm positioned behind her head.

The report notes that testing for sexual assault was performed but does not state whether evidence of an assault was detected.

Search-warrant applications released Friday allege that Carson was taken from her apartment, forced to give her abductors access to her bank account through an ATM and then fatally shot during the early morning hours of March 5.

The documents say that, in the days after Carson’s death, a confidential informant told investigators that Atwater had described how he and Lovette entered Carson’s residence through an unlocked or open door. According to the informant, the men then compelled Carson to leave with them in her own vehicle.

The informant said she spoke with Atwater after television stations broadcast an image of someone trying to use Carson’s ATM card at a convenience store two days after her body was discovered.

According to her account, the men drove Carson to an ATM and made her disclose her personal identification number. The court filings state: “The CW [informant] learned that Carson was forced into the back seat with Atwater, and Lovette drove Carson’s vehicle.” Investigators said this account matched video recorded by an ATM camera that day.

The witness also told police that Atwater claimed the men withdrew approximately $1,400 from Carson’s account. Court documents said bank records showed that roughly that amount had been removed over two days.

One affidavit says the informant reported that both men fired at Carson. Authorities said crime-scene findings supported that claim because evidence indicated that two different weapons were involved in the killing.

The warrant applications also said police believed Carson might have experienced a sexual assault “of an unknown nature,” and investigators requested permission to obtain DNA swabs from the suspects. However, Orange County District Attorney Jim Woodall told CNN on Friday that collecting and testing evidence from Carson’s body was standard procedure and that authorities did not believe she had been sexually assaulted.

Prosecutors initially sought to prevent the autopsy from becoming public. After the Raleigh News & Observer filed a motion seeking its disclosure, they agreed that the report could be released.

Carson, originally from Athens, Georgia, was preparing for medical studies and pursued two majors: biology and political science. UNC said she had received the university’s prestigious Morehead Scholarship and belonged to the Phi Beta Kappa honor society.

Carson, 22, was found March 5, 2008, on a street near the UNC-Chapel Hill campus. The autopsy concluded that she died from multiple gunshot wounds. Investigators said she had been shot with both a handgun and a shotgun.

According to warrants released by authorities, Carson was abducted from her home and forced into her blue Toyota Highlander. Surveillance images later showed attempts to use her bank card at automated teller machines, leading investigators to believe her captors forced her to withdraw money.

The documents say evidence recovered during the investigation—including ATM photographs, fingerprints and information from witnesses—helped authorities identify two suspects: Demario James Atwater and Laurence Alvin Lovette Jr. Both were charged with kidnapping and murder.

Investigators alleged that Atwater admitted taking part in the abduction and shooting, according to statements cited in the warrants. Prosecutors said Lovette also participated in the attack.

The autopsy found no evidence that Carson had been sexually assaulted, authorities said.

Carson, a senior from Athens, Georgia, was widely known on campus for her leadership and volunteer work. Her death prompted an outpouring of grief at UNC, where thousands attended a memorial service.

The released documents offer the most detailed official account to date of Carson’s final hours, while prosecutors continue to build their case against the two defendants.

# Court records, autopsy reveal new details in killing of UNC student leader Eve Carson

**CHAPEL HILL, N.C. —** University of North Carolina student body president Eve Carson was abducted from her Chapel Hill home, forced to withdraw money from automated teller machines and shot five times before her body was left in a residential neighborhood, according to newly released court documents and an autopsy report.

Carson, 22, was found shortly after 5 a.m. on March 5 near the intersection of Hillcrest Circle and Hillcrest Road, about a mile from the UNC-Chapel Hill campus. Police initially had few clues beyond her body and her missing sport-utility vehicle.

The records provide the clearest official account yet of the hours preceding her death. Investigators allege Carson was taken from her home early that morning and driven in her own vehicle to bank machines, where attempts were made to access her account. Surveillance photographs showed Carson at an ATM with another person nearby, authorities said.

The autopsy determined that Carson suffered four wounds from a handgun and a fatal shotgun wound to the head. The report listed the cause of death as multiple gunshot wounds and classified the death as a homicide. Some of the handgun wounds may not, by themselves, have been immediately fatal, according to the medical findings.

Authorities have charged **Demario James Atwater, 21, and Laurence Alvin Lovette Jr., 17**, with first-degree murder. They also face allegations connected to kidnapping, robbery and the theft of Carson’s vehicle. The charges are accusations, and neither defendant has been convicted.

Search-warrant affidavits and other court filings show that investigators relied on a combination of ATM images, cellphone records, witness statements and physical evidence to identify the suspects. Police also examined calls made from Carson’s phone after the killing and sought records that could establish where the device—and people associated with it—had been during the critical period.

According to the documents, witnesses told investigators that one or both suspects discussed the crime afterward. Authorities have not disclosed all of the evidence they believe links each defendant to the shooting, and some details in the filings remain allegations that will have to be tested in court.

Carson, a senior from Athens, Georgia, was studying political science and biology. She had been elected student body president in 2007 and was known across campus for her work on student government, public service and programs for children.

Her killing stunned the university community and prompted an outpouring of grief. Thousands attended a campus memorial, where friends, professors and fellow students remembered Carson as energetic, compassionate and deeply committed to helping others.

UNC officials said the release of additional details would be painful for those who knew her and urged the community to focus on her life rather than the violence of her death.

The investigation remains active as prosecutors prepare their cases against Atwater and Lovette. Authorities have said additional charges could be filed as the evidence is presented to grand juries and the cases move through state and federal courts.
